regressions.issue: Inside the inlined traverse loop, the slot whose key bytes were written to scratch memory once before the loop is no longer resolved. The list head, count and tail lose their mapping name and key (stor156[caller]) and print as hashes of unknown memory.
regressions.rule: Carry known memory words into a loop when the body writes no address that may alias them (the body's stores are all at or above the free-memory floor 0x80), so sha3(mem[0 len 64]) stays sha3(caller, 156), i.e. stor156[caller].

regressions.decompiled: if not t: revert with Panic(17) / if s != -1: s = s + 1; t = t - 1; u = ..; continue / break / (after the loop) revert with Panic(17)
regressions.issue: Both forms are exact (both checks raise Panic(17)), and the new order matches the source. But the itemCount overflow check now leaves the loop through a 'break' that falls to a revert after it, so the back edge is nested under 'if s != -1'. The same traverse inlined in unknownb15d2a2c keeps the two helper lines.
regressions.rule: Keep a check whose failing branch only reverts in place (if s == -1: revert ...) and do not route it through a loop exit; or print checked ++/-- with the helpers in their bytecode order.

summary: Mostly improved (P1 slot fixed, fake stor3 array resolved in unknownb15d2a2c, calls/logs/errors decoded). One regression: releaseStake's inlined traverse loop lost the stor156[caller] naming (12 lines of stor[sha3(mem[0 len 64])]), and its counter checks became a break-to-revert.
